## apps/exports

A document or a folder handed to a connected app as files,
for it to put where it works: a design into a repository.

inksprite writes nothing on the app's side, and is told no path there. It
makes the export ready and answers with a link, which the app's own shell
fetches, into wherever it runs the command: its own files, by its own
permissions, in a container as well as beside the app. The link is good
once, for a few minutes, and is all it takes, the connection's token
being nothing an app's model is ever shown (`electron/src/appExports.js`).

What is exported is what the app reads: nothing hidden from models, each
text as it stands without comments or suggestions, and stamped with the
document it came from (`files/exportStamp.js`). One file goes as itself,
more as a tar. A repository imported into the project is left out: its
files are where it came from, which is likely where the export is going.
A picture comes with the text that shows it only where the document it
belongs to is one the app sees in this project.

The command an answer gives is run by a shell we know nothing of, so
nothing in it is a name of the writer's making: a document's title may
have come from a web page or a file's name, and what quotes it for one
shell runs it in another. The file is saved under a plain name
(`plainName`), and the answer's `file` has the real one.

## quoted

The link as a shell takes it whole, whichever shell: sh and its kin,
PowerShell and cmd.exe all read double quotes, and cmd.exe reads no other.
A link is made here of an address the native side checked and an id of
letters, digits, dashes and underscores, so it holds nothing any of them
expands; one that held anything else is not put in a command.

### Parameters

- `link` **[string][164]**&#x20;

## plainName

A file's name as a command can hold it, with no quoting, in any shell: its
letters and digits, of any script, with `.`, `_` and `-`, and one `-` for
each run of anything else, a space or a quote among them. Never empty, and
never starting with a dot or a dash, which would hide the file or be read
as an option. The marks that are part of a letter in many scripts are kept
with it.

### Parameters

- `name` **[string][164]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][164]**&#x20;

## apps

Other apps on the same computer, working in the writer's
projects: a coding agent reading a design where it is written. In the
desktop app, which serves them over MCP. See `.llm/mcp_server_design.md`.

The native side is the door (`app/electron/src/appServer.js`): it listens,
checks who is asking against the connections the writer made
(Settings › Connections › Connected apps), and hands what an app asks to a
window. This module is what the asking means:

- **protocol** - MCP's requests answered, as far as tools go
- **tools** - The tools an app is offered, a chat's document tools with a
  project named on each, or only those that read for a connection that
  only reads, and a call to one run
- **projects** - The projects ticked for an app, by name, and a call run in
  one in the window that has it, or that takes it for the call
- **writes** - Several edits in one call, and an answer that says how the
  text was stored where that isn't how it was sent
- **revisions** - A revision on every read and write of a document, what
  the connection last had of it, and what has changed since
- **exports** - A document or a folder made ready as files, each text
  stamped with its document, for the app's own shell to fetch by a link

## inProject

Do something in a project, in this window, if this is the window to do it
in. The window that has the project open does it. With the project in no
window, this one takes it for as long as the work takes, as a job does
(`platform/windows.js`), reading it afresh if it hadn't had it, and saves
what the work wrote before letting go, for the next window to read. A
window that can't, because another has the project or has had it since
this one did, passes, and says which.

What is done in one project is done one thing at a time, in the order
asked: an app sends several calls at once, and two that write must not
cross.

### Parameters

- `storyId` **[string][164]**&#x20;
- `work` &#x20;

## apps/protocol

What a connected app asks, answered: MCP's requests, as far
as tools go. The desktop app's native side is the door
(`app/electron/src/appServer.js`): it knows who is asking, and hands the
request here whole, as the app sent it.

There are four to answer: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and
`tools/call`. No resources, prompts or sampling, no stream and no session:
a connection is told apart by its token alone, which the door has checked.

## apps/revisions

What a connected app has of a document, and what has changed
in it since.

A chat's model is told on every turn which of the documents it read have
changed (the project block's `changed`). An app is told nothing between
its calls, so its calls carry it: every read and write of a document
answers with the document's `revision`, a short hash of its text and its
comments as the connection reads them, and `changes_since` answers, for a
revision the app holds, what the writer has done since: the text as a
diff, what was said on its comments, and what became of the changes
suggested in it: which were accepted or rejected, what was said on them,
and which someone else has made since. That is the second round of a
review, without reading the document again.

To say what changed, what the connection last had of each document is
kept: its text and the state of its comments, by the native side
(`platform/apps.js`), on this computer. One record for each document, the
last, with the revisions the connection held on its way there: an app
holds the revision of its read while its own edits move the document on,
and asked with that one, it is told what has changed since the last of
them. A revision that is none of these can't be told from, and the app is
to read the document again.

A record is a copy of a document's text, so it is let go of when what it
is of goes: with its connection, with a project unticked for it, with a
document or a project deleted for good, and once the app has been told
that a document it had read is gone.

A write tells the app the revision it left. Where the document had
changed since the app last had it, besides the write, what is kept stays
as it was, and the answer says so: the app has not seen those changes,
and `changes_since` with the revision it held still shows them.

## apps/tools

The tools a connected app is offered, and a call to one run.

They are the document tools a chat's model has (`ai/tools/documents.js`),
by their names, each taking the project as well, since an app has several
where a chat has one, and `list_projects` for what those are. An app is
offered all of them, or only those that read, where its connection only
reads.

A chat's model gets more than its tools: the project block on every turn,
and a conversation the app can see. An app's gets only what a call
answers, so a few things differ here, and the tools themselves are left
as they are, their wording having been tuned for the chat:

- **A read always sends the text.** The app's context is its own, cut down
  and split among subagents out of our sight, so no call is handed the
  conversation, and none says a read is "still above".
- **The text comes as it is written**, in a part of the answer to itself
  after what is said about it, not as a string inside JSON: an edit quotes
  it exactly, and escaped line breaks and quotes get in the way of that.
- **Words written for outside.** Where a tool's description speaks of the
  project block, the chat, or tools an app isn't offered, the app is given
  another.
- **Several edits in a call, and how the text was stored** (`./writes.js`).
- **Documents handed over as files**: `export_document` makes a document
  or a folder ready and answers with a link the app's own shell fetches,
  each text stamped with the document it came from (`./exports.js`), and
  a document is reached by the id its stamp carries, written `id:<id>`
  where a path goes, whatever it has been renamed since: a document of the
  project named that the app sees, and no other.
- **A revision on every read and write, and what changed since one**
  (`./revisions.js`): what a chat's model is told on every turn of the
  documents it read, an app asks for.
- **A connection is who its comments are by**: its posts are a model's
  under the connection's name, which the Comments tab and other readers
  show.
- **A suggestion is asked for, call by call.** In a chat, whether edits
  wait is the chat's setting. Here it is how the app's own assistant was
  asked to work, so the three tools that change a document's text take
  `suggest`, true or false: the change is then laid out in the text, for
  the writer to accept or reject, as a chat that asks first has its. A
  plain document holds no such marks, and a suggestion to one is refused.
- **The suggestions waiting are listed where an app reads**, as they are
  for a chat: after a document's comments and among a list of them, its
  own and everyone else's, with what was said on each
  (`ai/tools/commentReads.js`). A chat's is said to be the assistant's,
  without the chat's title.

Hidden documents are not in an app's project, as they are not in a
chat's: hiding keeps a document from models. Nor is anything of the
writer's outside the projects ticked: their chats, their skills.

- `parameters` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;

## without

A text with a sentence taken out of it.

- `text` **[string][164]**&#x20;
- `sentence` **[string][164]**&#x20;

## EDIT_OUTSIDE

What `edit_document` says of itself to an app, which may send several edits.

Type: [string][164]

## SAID_OUTSIDE

What a tool says of itself to an app, where what it says to a chat's model
wouldn't be true there: given the tool as the chat has it, the description
or the parameters that differ.

## PROJECT

The argument every document tool takes of an app.

## LIST_PROJECTS_TOOL

Type: [AppTool][96]

## CHANGES_SINCE_TOOL

Type: [AppTool][96]

## EXPORT_DOCUMENT_TOOL

Type: [AppTool][96]

## OWN

The tools that are an app's alone, by name.

## offered

The tools an app is offered, by name, in the order it is told of them:
those that read, and, for a connection that writes, the rest. What changed
since comes after the tools that read, since it stands in for a read, and
the export after it: it changes nothing here, so every connection has it.

### Parameters

- `app` **AskingApp**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][167]<[string][164]>**&#x20;

## outside

A document tool as an app is told of it.

### Parameters

- `definition` &#x20;

Returns **[AppTool][96]**&#x20;

## toolsFor

The tools an app is offered.

### Parameters

- `app` **AskingApp**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][167]<[AppTool][96]>**&#x20;

## unsuggestable

Why a change to a document's text can't be suggested, or null where it
can: a plain document is kept as typed, and holds no marks for one. A path
with nothing at it is the tool's to turn down.

### Parameters

- `asking` **{storyId: [string][164], chatId: [string][164]}**&#x20;
- `path` **[string][164]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][165]<({error: [string][164]} | null)>**&#x20;

## sendsAll

Whether a read's answer sent the document's whole text, and not a slice,
a section or some lines of it.

### Parameters

- `answer` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;

## toResult

What a tool returned, as an app is answered. Text is sent as it is. A
document's text is a part to itself, after what is said about it and
before its comments. What went wrong is marked as an error, for the app's
model to read and act on.

### Parameters

- `value` **unknown**&#x20;

Returns **AppToolResult**&#x20;

##

Type: Record<[string][164], any>

## callTool

Run an app's call to a tool.

### Parameters

- `app` **AskingApp**&#x20;
- `name` **[string][164]** One of `toolsFor(app)`
- `args` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;
- `signal` **AbortSignal** Aborted when the app gives up on the call

## apps/writes

What a connected app's writes have that a chat's don't: several
edits in a call, and an answer that says how the text was stored when that
isn't how it was sent.

A chat's model makes one edit a call, and reads what it wrote back in the
conversation's own record. An app pays a round trip for each call, so it
may send `edits`, a list made in order as one write or not at all, and
`all`, for every place a passage appears. And it tends to edit from memory
of what it sent, where the document holds what the editor's Markdown made
of it: a table's spacing, a list's marker. So a write's answer carries the
passage as it now reads (`stored`) when that differs.

## STORED_MOST

Type: [number][163]

## STORED_MOST

One change to a passage, as an app asks for it.

Type: [number][163]

## STORED_MOST

The longest a stored passage is sent back, in characters; past it, the app is told to read.

Type: [number][163]

## STORED_NOTE

What a write's answer says when the text was stored another way than it was sent.

Type: [string][164]

## READ_AGAIN_NOTE

The same, where what changed is too long to send back.

Type: [string][164]

## textAt

A document's text as an app reads it, or null when there is none there.

### Parameters

- `context` **ToolContext**&#x20;
- `path` **[string][164]**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][165]<([string][164] | null)>**&#x20;

## editsOf

The edits a call asks for, each checked, or what is wrong with them.

### Parameters

- `args` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;

Returns **([Array][167]\<AppEdit> | {error: [string][164]})**&#x20;

## edits

Type: [Array][167]\<AppEdit>

## editMany

Change several passages of a document in one write, or every place a
passage appears. Each edit is made to the text the ones before it left,
and none is made unless all can be: a passage has to be there, and once
unless the edit says `all`.

The text is written as a whole body is (`update_document`), so the
writer's comments stay on the passages that come through unchanged, and
those whose words changed are resolved, as one edit does.

### Parameters

- `args` **Record<[string][164], any>** `path`, and `edits` or `old`, `new` and `all`
- `context` **ToolContext**&#x20;

Returns **[Promise][165]\<Record<[string][164], any>>**&#x20;

## sentBy

What a write sent to be in the document, by the tool that wrote it.

### Parameters

- `name` **[string][164]**&#x20;
- `args` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;

Returns **[Array][167]<[string][164]>**&#x20;

##

Type: any

## changedLines

The lines of a text that differ from what it was: from the first that
changed to the last, whole. Empty when nothing did.

### Parameters

- `before` **[string][164]**&#x20;
- `after` **[string][164]**&#x20;

Returns **[string][164]**&#x20;

## answeringStored

Run a write, and say in its answer how the text reads now where that is
not how it was sent: the lines that changed, or, where they are many, that
the document is to be read again. A write that was suggested says so too,
of the text as the app reads it, its suggestions made.

### Parameters

- `name` **[string][164]** The tool: one that writes a document's text
- `args` **Record<[string][164], any>**&#x20;
- `context` **ToolContext**&#x20;
- `write` &#x20;

Returns **[Promise][165]\<any>**&#x20;
